title: core.phys.colliders — approximate collision volumes
description: A sphere set and an oriented-box set, grouped per part. Cheap, universally supported primitives that every physics engine can consume without a cook step. A convex-decomposition mesh, when one exists, travels as its own GLB node and is linked by an 'enhances' edge; it is never required to make this node useful.

space.description: All primitives below are expressed in the local space of their group's part, i.e. after the part's transform chain from manifest parts[]. Declared because 'model space or part space' is exactly the question a reader must not have to guess.

material_id.description: Which surface material this volume represents, so an impact can pick the right sound and the right friction.

boxes.description: Oriented bounding boxes. Half-extents, not full extents; a rotation quaternion, not a matrix.

half_extents.description: metres, along the box's own axes

rotation.description: unit quaternion [w,x,y,z] taking box-local axes into part-local axes

convex_hull_node.description: Optional node_id of a GLB node holding a convex decomposition. An 'enhances' relationship only.

fit.description: How well these primitives approximate the real surface. Measured, so a consumer can decide whether to trust them for gameplay or only for broad phase.

hausdorff_max_m.description: Largest distance from any surface point of the source mesh to the collider union.

volume_ratio.description: collider union volume / source mesh volume. 1.0 is exact; above 1.0 is a fatter collider.
